derivation: The compliance is 1/(4 - x): it exceeds 1e5 exactly where 4 - x < 1e-5, i.e. x > 3.99999, and at x = 4 the gap is zero and the reading is +infinity, which is a real value of the expression rather than a failure to compute it - the rule still fails there, so the region runs up to and including the domain edge. The true failing set is x > 3.99999 with no upper bound at all: the model's own behaviour continues past the declared domain, and the region declared here is its intersection with the domain the instrument can sample, because a bound outside the declared domain cannot be checked against any point the grid will ever visit and used to be silently clamped. Declared share 1e-5 / 4 = 2.5e-6, matched to analytic/reciprocal_bound at 2e-6. This is also the entry where a channel blind to divergence is most exposed: the readings nearest the edge are non-finite, so the question the report asks is whether any arm calls that part of the domain trustworthy.

regions.reason: the deflection exceeds the allowed compliance at the stop

expect: a band pinned against the domain edge, whose far side cannot be seen
